headline: Count valid suffixes of a product window
statement: Count nonempty contiguous subarrays of positive nums whose product is strictly less than k.
intuition: Keep a continuous window whose product is below k. Multiply in the next value, then remove values from the left until the product qualifies. Every shorter suffix of that window also qualifies because all factors are at least 1. Count those suffixes by the window's length.
approach: Return zero when k <= 1 because every product is at least one.
Multiply in each right value and remove left values until product < k.
Add the number of valid suffixes ending at right.
correctness: After shrinking, the current window has product below k, while any earlier start would still be invalid. All later starts remove factors at least one, so they are valid. Each subarray has one right endpoint, so summing suffix counts counts every valid subarray once.
bruteForce: List all starting positions and multiply successive values; O(n²) time.

complexity.explanation: Each input factor enters and leaves the window at most once.

pitfalls: The inequality is strict, so shrink on product >= k.
Use integer division; floating-point rounding is unnecessary.
Zero or negative values are excluded and would change the reasoning.
